title: Municipal digital twin
challenge: Teams reason about the built environment from flat maps and site visits — with no shared, queryable 3D picture of the building stock.
built: A browser digital twin built on open 3DBAG building data, coloured live by real attributes (construction year, height, roof area). Self-hosted, no plugins, no external tiles. The model on this page is the real thing.
outcome: A real twin, in the browser
lesson: Bake the GIS offline and the runtime stays simple, fast and firewall-proof.

title: Alliander digital twin
challenge: Engineers evaluated transformer placement through repeated site visits — slow, and hard to coordinate.
built: A web-based spatial review platform combining industrial point clouds, 360° imagery and equipment previews, so engineers assess placement from their desk.
lesson: Product success depends on timing and organisational readiness, not technology alone — this one was ahead of it.

title: Alliander HoloLens suite
challenge: Crews place two-tonne transformers in neighbourhoods where centimetres matter, with no way to see the planned position on the real ground.
built: A HoloLens suite combining RTK GPS, an Android correction device, backend services and reporting portals to visualise transformer placement at centimetre accuracy, on-site.
lesson: The technical challenge was only half the problem; integrating with the organisation's processes was the other half.

title: Niantic Explorer platform
challenge: Events wanted geospatial AR anchored to real places — reliably, and at scale.
built: A location-based AR platform (first used at SXSW, Austin) using GPS and Visual Positioning Systems to place content in the world.
lesson: Location-based AR is a systems-integration problem; real-world localisation is hard and UX matters more than capability.

title: Virtuele Brigade
challenge: A training simulator already years into development needed multiplayer networking and new VR training — without destabilising the existing codebase.
built: Refactored the architecture to integrate multiplayer VR and a scenario configurator, so instructors author and run training scenarios. Demonstrated regularly at events.
lesson: Adding technology to a live system is often harder than building from scratch — reliability beats elegance.

title: Lightship Drive
challenge: Showcase shared AR and Visual Positioning Systems as a live, multiplayer racing experience on a trade-show floor.
built: A multiplayer AR racing game with spectator modes, external displays, synchronised audio and server infrastructure.
lesson: Test the whole chain, not individual components — build around failure instead of assuming perfect conditions.

title: Zwijsen AR books
challenge: Link physical educational books to digital AR and audio — shipped and supported at consumer scale.
built: Designed, built and published educational AR and audiobook apps linked to printed books via QR codes, across iOS and Android.
lesson: End-to-end ownership teaches the whole product lifecycle, from design to distribution.

title: Popcore hyper-casual games
challenge: Ship hyper-casual mobile hits at pace, with gameplay, multiplayer and designer tools a team can iterate on daily.
built: Built gameplay features, multiplayer and designer tooling within an ECS architecture for titles including Parking Jam, Pull the Pin and Wrecking Ball.
lesson: Product performance and iteration speed often matter more than technical purity.

title: Philips medical XR & AI
challenge: Find where emerging XR and AI actually help in a clinical context — and demonstrate medical equipment compellingly.
built: A synthetic-data project for remote heartbeat detection using Unreal Engine and computer vision, alongside VR equipment demonstrations and Apple Vision Pro exploration.
lesson: Research is as much about discovering what should not be built as what should.

title: Amsterdam AI prototype
challenge: Explore AI-driven AR tour guides that voice the perspectives of fictional residents — end to end.
built: A prototype combining speech recognition, language models, text-to-speech, facial animation and generated characters into conversational AR guides.
lesson: Automating everything can remove the human element; feasibility doesn't guarantee emotional value.

title: Custom AR framework
challenge: Before AR Foundation existed, ARCore and ARKit were separate worlds — cross-platform AR meant maintaining two codebases.
built: A framework unifying ARCore and ARKit behind one API, investigating cloud anchors and cross-platform compatibility.
lesson: Building foundational tools often creates more value than solving individual problems.
